mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 8% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 8% but SPX shows positive 20-day returns more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS are high and UNRATE is low, it may indicate a tightening cycle, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE meet the trigger but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 30%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production in an expansion signals continued economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth is strong but SPX returns are negative over 60 days more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm employment signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 5 days more than 50%.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in housing starts indicates reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth is negative but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real federal funds rate indicates easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS decreases but SPX returns are negative over 60 days more than 50%.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI inflation may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL exceeds 220 but SPX returns are positive over 20 days more than 30%.
